label: Ukraine GDP Change 2022
change: Largest single-year drop in modern Ukrainian history

label: Ukraine GDP Growth 2023
change: Partial recovery driven by defense industry and western aid

label: Ukraine Reconstruction Cost Estimate
change: Needed over 10 years; equivalent to 3× pre-war Ukrainian GDP

label: Frozen Russian State Assets
change: Primarily €210B at Euroclear Belgium; generating ~$3B/year interest

label: US Military Aid to Ukraine (total)
change: Includes Biden-era packages + $61B April 2024 package; minerals deal (Apr 2025) counts future US military aid as fund contributions

label: EU Total Aid to Ukraine (all types)
change: EU surpassed US as largest single aid provider in 2024; includes €50B 4-year facility. NATO targeting additional $15B for Ukraine in 2026.
source: Kiel Institute for the World Economy (Feb 2026)

label: Russia Defense Spending (% of GDP)
change: Up from 3.6% pre-war; 41% of all federal budget on military/security

label: Russian Central Bank Interest Rate
change: Cut from 21% peak (7th cut since Jun 2025); Bank of Russia easing cycle — 15.5% Feb 2026, then 15% Mar 20, 2026 as economy slows and inflation moderates to ~5.9%. Oil export disruptions from Ukrainian drone campaign compound economic pressure.

label: Ukraine War Cost per Day (Russia)
change: Estimated daily Russian war expenditure; driving budget deficit and depleting National Wealth Fund

label: Russian National Wealth Fund
change: Kremlin acknowledged fund running dry; at record withdrawal pace in early 2026. ~40% of Russian oil export capacity halted (Mar 25) from Ukrainian drone strikes on Ust-Luga and Primorsk ports plus tanker seizures — described as most severe disruption in modern Russian history.

label: Ukrainians in Poverty
change: Up from 5.5% pre-war; 7.1M pushed into poverty

label: G7 Loan to Ukraine (backed by frozen assets)
change: Finalized Oct 2024; US contributed $20B; secured by Russian asset interest (~$3B/year)

label: Brent Crude Oil Price
change: Surged above $100 for first time since 2022 invasion; driven by Iran-US conflict closing Strait of Hormuz. US Treasury issued 30-day waiver on Russian seaborne crude Mar 13, 2026.

label: US–Ukraine Critical Minerals Investment Fund
change: Joint fund for Ukraine reconstruction backed by future mineral revenues. Future US military aid counts as US contribution. Ukraine not required to repay past aid. Minerals wealth estimated at $14.8T total.

label: Russia Gasoline Export Ban (April 2026)
change: Russia suspended all gasoline exports effective April 1, 2026 — direct consequence of Ukrainian drone strikes cutting domestic refining capacity and port export throughput
source: Russian Deputy PM Novak / Reuters / Bloomberg (Mar 30, 2026)

label: EU 20th Sanctions Package + €90B Ukraine Loan
change: EU formally adopted 20th Russia sanctions (120+ new listings, 20 banks, 46 shadow fleet tankers now 632 total, crypto platform ban, anti-circumvention tool vs. Kyrgyzstan) and approved €90B interest-free loan to Ukraine on April 23, 2026 — covering two-thirds of Ukraine's needs through 2027-28

label: Zelensky Demands EU 21st Sanctions Package
change: Following Russia's 666-asset mass attack, Zelensky formally called on EU leaders to immediately advance a 21st sanctions package against Russia — one day after the 20th package entered into force (Apr 23). The new package would target additional energy revenues and shadow fleet tankers.

label: Russia GDP Contraction Q1 2026
change: Russia's economy contracted 0.3% in Q1 2026 — first quarterly GDP decline since early 2023 — under combined pressure of war expenditure, Western sanctions, and the Bank of Russia's high interest rates. 2026 full-year forecast downgraded to 0.4% from 1.3%.

label: Ukraine Strikes Novorossiysk Oil Terminal (May 23)
change: Ukraine struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal and Grushovaya oil depot at Novorossiysk — Russia's largest Black Sea crude export hub handling ~75 million tons/year (~20% of Russia's total crude exports). Shadow-fleet tanker 'Chrysalis' also hit. Fires confirmed at both facilities. Compounds disruptions from Ukraine's March–May 2026 campaign targeting Baltic oil ports (Ust-Luga, Primorsk) and Black Sea refineries (Tuapse struck 4 times).
source: Bloomberg / Kyiv Independent / Fortune / The Moscow Times (May 23, 2026)

label: Ukraine Strikes Vtorovo Oil Station (Vladimir Oblast) — Moscow Airport Fuel Supply Hit
change: Ukraine's SBU Special Group Alpha drones struck the Vtorovo oil pumping and dispatching station in Vladimir Oblast (JSC Transneft Verkhnyaya Volga) — the facility pumps diesel into the Moscow Ring Oil Product Pipeline, directly supplying Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, and Vnukovo airports. 800 sq meter fire, heavy smoke. Second strike on this facility (first: Sep 2025). Part of Ukraine's 'long-range sanctions' campaign deepening into Russia's domestic fuel supply chains.

label: Ukraine Strikes Armavir Oil Depot + Taganrog Shadow Tanker (May 30)
change: Ukraine's long-range drones struck the Armavir oil depot in Krasnodar Krai (~500 km from border) and a shadow-fleet sanctions-evasion tanker in Taganrog port on the night of May 29–30. Zelensky confirmed both strikes plus a simultaneous hit on a marine oil terminal in occupied Crimea. Armavir attack expands Ukraine's 2026 energy campaign beyond refineries into oil storage and distribution hubs — third Krasnodar Krai energy target struck in 2026 after Ilsky refinery (March 27) and Tuapse refinery (April 16, 20). Combined with Novorossiysk (May 23), Volgograd Lukoil (May 29), Vtorovo (May 24), and Baltic terminal strikes (March 2026), Ukraine's energy infrastructure campaign has struck ~12 Russian facilities in 2026 alone.

label: Ukraine Strikes Saratov Refinery + Kirov Pipeline Station (June 1)
change: Ukraine's overnight May31-Jun1 drone campaign (229 drones; 212 intercepted) struck the Rosneft Saratov oil refinery on the Volga River (~700km from front; ~7M ton/year capacity; large-scale fire confirmed) and the Lazarevo pumping station in Kirov region (~1,300km from Ukraine), which serves the Surgut-Gorky-Polotsk pipeline transporting Siberian crude oil to Belarus. Two new Russian regions struck in a single night — expanding Ukraine's energy offensive to Saratov and Kirov oblasts in addition to prior strikes across Krasnodar, Volgograd, Yaroslavl, Moscow, Ryazan, and Leningrad regions.
source: Japan Times / Al Jazeera / Ukraine General Staff (June 1, 2026)

label: EU €90B Loan First Tranche — Approaching Ukraine
change: The European Union is preparing to deliver the first tranche of its €90 billion interest-free loan to Ukraine in late May/early June 2026, specifically earmarked for weapons purchases including air defense interceptors, artillery ammunition, and drone mass production. The loan was approved on April 23, 2026 (20th sanctions package) and covers approximately two-thirds of Ukraine's defense needs through 2027–2028. First tranche delivery represents the most significant European defense financing of 2026 — arriving as Ukraine's air defense interceptors reach critical shortage levels following Russia's May 2026 mass aerial campaign.

label: Ukraine Strikes Ilsky Refinery (16th Time) — Krasnodar Energy Disruption
change: Ukraine struck the Ilsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai for at least the 16th time since the start of the full-scale invasion, igniting a large fire visible 10+ km away (capacity: ~6.6M tonnes/year). The strike is part of Ukraine's sustained June 2026 energy campaign following June 1 strikes on the Saratov Rosneft refinery (~7M ton/year) and Kirov Lazarevo pipeline station (~1,300 km from Ukraine), May 30 strikes on Armavir oil depot and Taganrog shadow tanker, and May 23 Novorossiysk terminal strike. Ukraine also destroyed a Pantsir-S1 air defense system and struck a Russian vessel in Crimea in the same operational window.

label: Germany €11.5B Ukraine Aid Package (June 2026)
change: Germany announced its largest-ever single-country Ukraine aid package of €11.5 billion in June 2026 — focused on air defense systems (Patriot, IRIS-T), drones, and artillery ammunition. Combined with Norway's ~$7B commitment and the NATO $15B 2026 target, European military financing for Ukraine reached record levels even as US Congress advanced the Ukraine Support Act ($8B) — reflecting the shift of primary Western Ukraine support responsibility to European nations.

label: US Senate Passes 100% Tariff Sanctions Bill on Russian Oil Buyers
change: The US Senate passed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in early August 2026, authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue purchasing Russian oil and gas. Zelensky welcomed the move, saying 'real, strong American pressure and sanctions against Russia are what will help the most' to end the war. The bill adds to mounting economic pressure on Moscow: Russia's economy contracted 0.6% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 2026, and oil and gas revenues in H1 2026 were just 64% of their level two years earlier, amid a lower EU oil price cap and sustained Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.
source: US Senate / Al Jazeera / KSE Institute (Aug 2026)

label: Ukraine Downgrades 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to 0.5% Amid Russian Strikes
change: Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko said on August 26 that Ukraine's Economy Ministry is downgrading its 2026 GDP growth forecast from 1.3% to roughly 0.5%, citing Russian strikes on energy and logistics infrastructure and the Black Sea port blockade — Ukraine's main export route. Kravchenko said the impact of Russian shelling alone is estimated at up to 0.5 percentage points of expected growth. Affected sectors include steel production, e-commerce, ports, energy, and agriculture (17% of GDP). The downgrade follows a sustained Ukrainian and Russian deep-strike campaign against each other's energy and logistics infrastructure through August 2026.
source: Ukraine Ministry of Economy / Kyiv Independent (Aug 26, 2026)
